findings.title: Handle events with no destination calendar before checking the integration
findings.body: When `destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array, destructuring leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined and this dereference throws. A Google Meet booking without a configured destination calendar therefore fails during event creation instead of taking the fallback path that existed before this change.

findings.title: Select the Lark destination belonging to the credential being used
findings.body: Collective creation invokes the calendar service once per destination using that host's credential, but this always selects the first destination in the whole event. For later hosts, the service attempts to create the event in the first host's Lark calendar, which can fail due to permissions or create it in the wrong calendar. Select the destination whose `credentialId` matches this service's credential.

findings.title: Select the Office 365 destination belonging to the credential being used
findings.body: Collective creation invokes this service once per host credential, but this always uses the first destination calendar in the event. A later host's Office 365 account will consequently target the first host's calendar ID, which may be inaccessible or cause the event to be written to the wrong calendar. Choose the destination associated with the current credential.

findings.title: Create CalDAV events in the destination for the current credential
findings.body: The event is filtered to the first destination calendar regardless of which credential is creating it. Since collective event creation calls the service for each host, each CalDAV account targets the first host's calendar URL; other hosts' events can fail or be created in the wrong calendar. Match the destination to the current credential before filtering.

findings.title: Use the matching destination calendar for the Google organizer attendee
findings.body: For a collective event, this code uses the first host's destination calendar as the organizer email in every host's event copy. When creating or updating the copy for another credential, the organizer therefore refers to a different host's calendar instead of the calendar associated with that credential, which can produce incorrect organizer details or cause Google to reject the event. Select the destination matching the current credential (and do the same in `updateEvent`).

findings.title: Restore a calendar fallback when updating or deleting without an external ID
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is absent, the lookup compares each calendar's `externalId` to that same absent value and returns `undefined`; it never falls back to the event's destination calendar. Updates then send an undefined `calendarId`, and deletes fall through to `primary`, potentially failing to update or deleting from the wrong calendar for legacy references without an external calendar ID.
